transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

The most likely cause is a slipped or snapped drive belt: the machine can sound as though it is running while the drum stays still. Less commonly, the motor is only humming because its start capacitor has failed, or the drum is being held by an obstruction/support fault. 1. Switch it off, unplug it and empty it. Turn the drum slowly by hand. - Turns very freely with little resistance: suggests the drive belt has come off or broken. - Turns smoothly with normal resistance: could still be belt-related, or a motor/capacitor issue. - Feels stiff, rough, or will barely move: something may be jammed, or a drum roller/bearing needs attention. 2. Check the load as well: a single heavy item or overfull drum can prevent proper tumbling. Remove items and try only a few light towels afterwards. Do not keep running it with the drum stationary, as clothes will not dry properly and the appliance can overheat. Tell me how the empty drum feels when turned by hand; that will separate a belt fault from a motor or drum-support fault.
unplugged it and turned the drum by hand and it spins really easy almost no resistance. also heard a twang then thud yesterday mid cycle and a slight rubber smell at the time

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That pattern points very strongly to the drum drive belt having snapped or come off. The twang/thud was likely the belt letting go, and the rubber smell can happen as it slips or breaks. The underlying cause may simply be an aged belt, but an engineer should also inspect the jockey/idler tension pulley and drum supports: a seized or worn pulley can damage a new belt. A motor capacitor is much less likely because the noise and sudden change during the cycle fit a belt failure better. Do not use the dryer again. With the rubber smell and a running motor with no drum movement, it needs a qualified appliance engineer to inspect and repair the belt-drive system before it is used.

candidates: Motor start capacitor or motor drive fault (medium)
Drum obstruction or worn drum support/bearing (low)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Drive belt has snapped or come off (high)
Jockey/idler pulley failure causing the belt to fail or come off (medium)
